components.gap: Definitions and source variant not plainly supplied. The entry defines only the expected logarithmic loss L_p(q) on one finite outcome set (body 446-450). Its final claim (body 457-459) says the cumulative conditional logarithmic score is -log m_n(x_{1:n}), but no realized logarithmic score of a report at an outcome, and no cumulative conditional score as a sum over the predictive factors r_i, is defined in the entry or the chapter; the title's 'logarithmic score' is never tied to the defined loss. The cited Kass-Raftery Sec. 3.2 presentation (held PDF p. 6, journal p. 777) defines the logarithmic scoring rule as log pr_i(y_i), the overall score LS = sum_i log pr_i(y_i), and log pr(D|H_k) = LS_k, which is the reward orientation. The entry neither preserves that variant nor states that its score has the opposite sign, so read with the cited source's definition the displayed value -log m_n carries the wrong sign.

defect_observations.observation: Writable fix for the partial verdict: define the realized logarithmic loss -log q(y) and the cumulative conditional score -sum_i log r_i(x_i | x_{1:i-1}), then state that Kass-Raftery's LS = sum_i log pr_i(y_i) is its negative, so that LS = log m_n.

The entry uses m^w, Pi^w_x, Pi_x w, Pi^eps_x and R_x without defining them; m^w is computed only at annex 400-401 and listed in the P01 notation register (handbook/parts/p01/notation-binding-and-comparison-of-formal-w02-p01-024.tex line 1571). The contamination paragraph (340-347) relies on the earlier 'regular observation' (line 326) for 0 < m(x) < infinity without restating it; the mixture formula would fail where m(x) is infinite, a marginal-null set. Not scored as a gap because the fixed regular observation carries through the theorem.

The constant terms of the square identity are said to agree after being put over a common denominator, but that computation is not written out. The theta-squared and theta coefficients are verified with reasons. This is the one unwritten algebraic step in the proof, and it is routine.

The body clause concerns replacing the predictive factors r_i by unconditional one-observation marginals. The annex argues it through the copied flag ('can produce a different posterior'; the second positive has conditional probability one under either state). That gives r_2 = 1 against an unconditional marginal 1098/100000, but the comparison is stated only in words and speaks of a posterior rather than of the evidence m_n.

E(theta^2 | x) comes from 'the beta recurrence, obtained from the beta-gamma identity', and the recurrence itself is not displayed. The beta mean and variance it rests on are stated and proved in thm:p15-beta-gamma-convolution (handbook/parts/p15/convolution-gamma-normal.tex 250-279).
